decision.reason: Three repeated shared failures justified 0.1.2. Its residual unlabeled-message grouping error justified the narrower 0.1.3 rule, which passed all three repetitions of a new four-message forward test.

limitations: All materials were synthetic; no real chats, accounts, people, screenshots, or private relationship data were used.
Explicit project-level skill invocation measured loaded instruction value, not implicit routing; the trace-based implicit gate remains unpassed.
The reviewer was a separate Codex model task, not an independent human relationship expert.
For the 0.1.2 and 0.1.3 focused runs, the reviewer had inspected the protocol and revision before generation, although it remained blind to the random candidate-to-arm key while scoring.
Repeated outputs from six, three, and one synthetic tasks do not establish a general relationship-advice ranking.
The first verbal-notice criterion was recognized post-reveal as over-specific; its frozen score remains unchanged, and the later test used a different scenario with a semantic criterion.
The final 0.1.3 advantage on speaker mapping is based on one new task repeated three times and needs broader future forward testing.
